title: Biodiversity and Human Impact Core Test
description: Core practice for biodiversity, ecosystem services, human impacts, evidence-based solutions, and tradeoffs.

questions.prompt: What does biodiversity mean?
questions.questionText: What does biodiversity mean?
options: the variety of life in an ecosystem
the amount of sunlight only
one organism living alone
the number of buildings near a habitat
questions.correctAnswer: the variety of life in an ecosystem
questions.explanation: Biodiversity means variety of life, including species, genetic variation, and ecosystem roles.

questions.prompt: Which ecosystem likely has higher biodiversity?
questions.questionText: Which ecosystem likely has higher biodiversity?
options: a lawn with one grass species only
a meadow with many plant, insect, bird, and soil organism species
a parking lot with no plants
a sealed jar with only sand
questions.correctAnswer: a meadow with many plant, insect, bird, and soil organism species
questions.explanation: The meadow has more kinds of organisms and roles.

questions.prompt: Which is an ecosystem service?
questions.questionText: Which is an ecosystem service?
options: plastic wrappers entering a stream
a road splitting habitat
wetlands filtering water
a pollutant killing algae
questions.correctAnswer: wetlands filtering water
questions.explanation: Ecosystem services are benefits ecosystems provide, such as clean water.

questions.prompt: A garden with many plant species survives a disease better than a one-species garden. Which claim is best supported?
questions.questionText: A garden with many plant species survives a disease better than a one-species garden. Which claim is best supported?
options: Biodiversity always prevents every problem.
One species is always safest.
Disease proves plants are nonliving.
Biodiversity can make a system more resilient.
questions.correctAnswer: Biodiversity can make a system more resilient.
questions.explanation: Variety can provide resilience when one species is affected.

questions.prompt: Which model best shows human impact on biodiversity?
questions.questionText: Which model best shows human impact on biodiversity?
options: human action -> habitat/resource change -> population effects -> possible solution
biodiversity -> no organisms -> no evidence
solution -> no problem -> no data
species -> road -> no interactions
questions.correctAnswer: human action -> habitat/resource change -> population effects -> possible solution
questions.explanation: A useful model connects actions, ecosystem changes, effects, and solutions.

questions.prompt: A wetland receives fertilizer runoff. Algae increases, oxygen drops, and fish decrease. What solution targets the cause most directly?
questions.questionText: A wetland receives fertilizer runoff. Algae increases, oxygen drops, and fish decrease. What solution targets the cause most directly?
options: paint the fish a brighter color
reduce nutrient runoff before it enters the wetland
count fish without changing runoff
add more road signs near the wetland
questions.correctAnswer: reduce nutrient runoff before it enters the wetland
questions.explanation: The cause is nutrient runoff, so a strong solution targets runoff.

questions.prompt: Which evidence best shows a biodiversity loss?
questions.questionText: Which evidence best shows a biodiversity loss?
options: A map uses green ink.
The park has a new sign.
The number of native plant species drops from 18 to 6 after development.
One bird is photographed twice.
questions.correctAnswer: The number of native plant species drops from 18 to 6 after development.
questions.explanation: A drop in species count is evidence of biodiversity loss.

questions.prompt: A student says, "Biodiversity only means number of species." Which correction is best?
questions.questionText: A student says, "Biodiversity only means number of species." Which correction is best?
options: It means only the number of rocks.
It means only the amount of water.
It means all organisms are identical.
It also includes genetic variation and different ecosystem roles.
questions.correctAnswer: It also includes genetic variation and different ecosystem roles.
questions.explanation: Biodiversity includes more than species count.

questions.prompt: Which design solution best addresses animals being hit while crossing a road through habitat?
questions.questionText: Which design solution best addresses animals being hit while crossing a road through habitat?
options: a wildlife crossing placed where tracking data show animals cross
a poster far from the road only
removing all plants from the habitat
counting cars without changing the crossing problem
questions.correctAnswer: a wildlife crossing placed where tracking data show animals cross
questions.explanation: A wildlife crossing targets habitat fragmentation and should be placed using evidence.

questions.prompt: Which tradeoff should be considered before building a wildlife crossing?
questions.questionText: Which tradeoff should be considered before building a wildlife crossing?
options: whether the word crossing has two syllables
cost, location, and whether animals will actually use it
whether all ecosystems are identical
whether evidence should be ignored
questions.correctAnswer: cost, location, and whether animals will actually use it
questions.explanation: Engineering solutions should consider tradeoffs and evidence.

questions.prompt: An invasive plant shades native pond plants. Insects that rely on native plants decrease. Which chain best explains the effect?
questions.questionText: An invasive plant shades native pond plants. Insects that rely on native plants decrease. Which chain best explains the effect?
options: invasive plant -> more native light -> more insects only
insects choose to become plants
invasive plant -> less light for natives -> fewer native plants -> fewer insects
shade creates new fish from nothing
questions.correctAnswer: invasive plant -> less light for natives -> fewer native plants -> fewer insects
questions.explanation: The invasive species changes resources, which affects other populations.

questions.prompt: Which evidence would best test whether a restoration project is working?
questions.questionText: Which evidence would best test whether a restoration project is working?
options: the color of the project folder
one person's favorite animal
the number of pencils used
native species counts before restoration and for several seasons after
questions.correctAnswer: native species counts before restoration and for several seasons after
questions.explanation: Before-and-after species data can show whether biodiversity changes.

questions.prompt: A forest has many tree species. A pest attacks one tree species. Why might the forest keep more functions than a one-species forest?
questions.questionText: A forest has many tree species. A pest attacks one tree species. Why might the forest keep more functions than a one-species forest?
options: Other tree species can still provide habitat and resources.
All pests disappear in diverse forests.
Only one species ever matters.
Tree species do not interact with ecosystems.
questions.correctAnswer: Other tree species can still provide habitat and resources.
questions.explanation: Diversity can provide alternate resources and roles.

questions.prompt: Which human action most directly fragments habitat?
questions.questionText: Which human action most directly fragments habitat?
options: recording bird songs
building a highway through a continuous forest
planting native shrubs
removing litter from a stream
questions.correctAnswer: building a highway through a continuous forest
questions.explanation: A highway can split a habitat into smaller pieces.

questions.prompt: Which claim is strongest for a proposed solution to runoff?
questions.questionText: Which claim is strongest for a proposed solution to runoff?
options: The solution sounds nice.
The solution has a short name.
Buffer plants near streams reduced nitrate levels in similar test sites.
The solution is shown in blue ink.
questions.correctAnswer: Buffer plants near streams reduced nitrate levels in similar test sites.
questions.explanation: Evidence from similar tests strengthens a design claim.

questions.prompt: A city replaces native plants with pavement. Which impact is most likely?
questions.questionText: A city replaces native plants with pavement. Which impact is most likely?
options: more nesting places for every species
no change to water flow or habitat
instant increase in all biodiversity
less habitat and fewer resources for some local organisms
questions.correctAnswer: less habitat and fewer resources for some local organisms
questions.explanation: Pavement can reduce habitat and change water movement.

questions.prompt: Which model revision improves this chain: people build houses -> fewer animals?
questions.questionText: Which model revision improves this chain: people build houses -> fewer animals?
options: houses -> habitat loss and fragmentation -> fewer resources and movement paths -> some populations decrease
houses -> animals choose to vanish
houses -> more forest inside every yard
houses -> no ecosystem changes
questions.correctAnswer: houses -> habitat loss and fragmentation -> fewer resources and movement paths -> some populations decrease
questions.explanation: The improved model explains the mechanisms connecting development to population effects.

questions.prompt: A student claims, "Any solution that helps one species is automatically best." What is the best response?
questions.questionText: A student claims, "Any solution that helps one species is automatically best." What is the best response?
options: Helping one species always solves every ecosystem problem.
A solution should consider ecosystem effects, evidence, and tradeoffs.
Tradeoffs are never part of design.
Evidence makes solutions worse.
questions.correctAnswer: A solution should consider ecosystem effects, evidence, and tradeoffs.
questions.explanation: Solutions can have tradeoffs and should be evaluated with evidence.

questions.prompt: Which data pattern suggests pollution may be reducing stream biodiversity?
questions.questionText: Which data pattern suggests pollution may be reducing stream biodiversity?
options: The stream name changes.
The sampling jars are the same size.
Sensitive insect species decrease as pollutant levels increase.
The stream is shown on a map.
questions.correctAnswer: Sensitive insect species decrease as pollutant levels increase.
questions.explanation: A pattern linking pollution increase and sensitive species decrease supports the claim.

questions.prompt: Why can genetic variation within one species matter for conservation?
questions.questionText: Why can genetic variation within one species matter for conservation?
options: It makes every individual identical.
It removes the need for habitat.
It proves ecosystems have no interactions.
It can help a population include traits that may handle future changes.
questions.correctAnswer: It can help a population include traits that may handle future changes.
questions.explanation: Variation within a species can support resilience when conditions change.

questions.prompt: A wetland restoration increases native plants, insects, and nesting birds over three years. Which claim is best supported?
questions.questionText: A wetland restoration increases native plants, insects, and nesting birds over three years. Which claim is best supported?
options: The restoration may be improving habitat and biodiversity.
The restoration harmed every species.
Only one organism changed once.
The data are unrelated to biodiversity.
questions.correctAnswer: The restoration may be improving habitat and biodiversity.
questions.explanation: Multiple native groups increasing over time supports improvement.

questions.prompt: Which question best evaluates an engineering design for fish passage around a dam?
questions.questionText: Which question best evaluates an engineering design for fish passage around a dam?
options: Is the dam name easy to remember?
Do fish counts upstream increase after the passage is installed?
What color is the sign?
Can the passage be drawn in one line?
questions.correctAnswer: Do fish counts upstream increase after the passage is installed?
questions.explanation: Fish movement data directly tests whether the passage helps.

questions.prompt: Which scenario shows a human action protecting biodiversity?
questions.questionText: Which scenario shows a human action protecting biodiversity?
options: draining a wetland for parking
releasing an invasive plant
planting connected native habitat corridors between isolated patches
dumping fertilizer into a pond
questions.correctAnswer: planting connected native habitat corridors between isolated patches
questions.explanation: Habitat corridors can support movement and connected populations.

questions.prompt: A solution removes all dead logs from a forest to make it look tidy. Which ecosystem role might be harmed?
questions.questionText: A solution removes all dead logs from a forest to make it look tidy. Which ecosystem role might be harmed?
options: sunlight itself
rock layers only
the number of road lanes
decomposers and organisms that use dead wood as habitat
questions.correctAnswer: decomposers and organisms that use dead wood as habitat
questions.explanation: Dead wood supports decomposers and habitat for many organisms.

questions.prompt: Which statement best handles uncertainty in human-impact claims?
questions.questionText: Which statement best handles uncertainty in human-impact claims?
options: The data suggest a link, but more controlled evidence can test the cause.
A pattern always proves the exact cause.
Uncertainty means no evidence matters.
Controlled comparisons are useless.
questions.correctAnswer: The data suggest a link, but more controlled evidence can test the cause.
questions.explanation: Careful science distinguishes patterns from proven causes.

questions.prompt: A biodiversity index rises after native plants are restored. What does the index most likely summarize?
questions.questionText: A biodiversity index rises after native plants are restored. What does the index most likely summarize?
options: only the color of flowers
variety and relative abundance of organisms in the ecosystem
only the number of park benches
only the amount of pavement
questions.correctAnswer: variety and relative abundance of organisms in the ecosystem
questions.explanation: Biodiversity measures often summarize variety and abundance.

questions.prompt: Which solution best addresses an invasive fish reducing native fish populations?
questions.questionText: Which solution best addresses an invasive fish reducing native fish populations?
options: add more invasive fish
ignore population data
remove or control the invasive fish while monitoring native populations
remove all water from every habitat
questions.correctAnswer: remove or control the invasive fish while monitoring native populations
questions.explanation: The solution targets the cause and includes monitoring evidence.

questions.prompt: A city wants both flood protection and wildlife habitat. Which design is most aligned with ecosystem services?
questions.questionText: A city wants both flood protection and wildlife habitat. Which design is most aligned with ecosystem services?
options: pave the entire floodplain
remove all streamside plants
build only walls and never monitor effects
restore wetlands that absorb floodwater and support native species
questions.correctAnswer: restore wetlands that absorb floodwater and support native species
questions.explanation: Wetlands can provide flood control and habitat benefits.

questions.prompt: Which evidence would weaken the claim that a new park design improved biodiversity?
questions.questionText: Which evidence would weaken the claim that a new park design improved biodiversity?
options: Species richness stayed the same and several native populations declined after installation.
The park has a sign.
The design map is colorful.
Visitors like the walking path.
questions.correctAnswer: Species richness stayed the same and several native populations declined after installation.
questions.explanation: No improvement or declining native populations would weaken the biodiversity claim.

questions.prompt: Which final explanation best shows biodiversity and human-impact understanding?
questions.questionText: Which final explanation best shows biodiversity and human-impact understanding?
options: Biodiversity is just one species count.
Biodiversity supports ecosystem resilience, human actions can change habitats and resources, and strong solutions use evidence plus tradeoff analysis.
Any helpful-sounding action is best.
Human impacts never ripple through ecosystems.
questions.correctAnswer: Biodiversity supports ecosystem resilience, human actions can change habitats and resources, and strong solutions use evidence plus tradeoff analysis.
questions.explanation: This connects biodiversity, impact chains, evidence, and design tradeoffs.
